content.user_title: Compare US Walk, Transit, and Bike Scores
content.value_statement: Comparing mobility scores across US locations requires repeated lookups. This skill submits grouped requests to an Apify Actor and retrieves scores, rating labels, and amenity categories.
actual_capabilities: Submit US address, city, neighborhood, state, or national ranking lookups through five documented Actor modes.
Retrieve declared Walk Score, Transit Score, Bike Score, rating description, and nearby amenity fields.
Request city neighborhood tables with includeNeighborhoods and configure record limits with maxItems.
Run the Node 18+ helper with a JSON file, inline JSON, or the bundled example input.
Retrieve synchronous JSON results or follow documented asynchronous run and dataset retrieval steps.
limitations: Requires an Apify account, APIFY_TOKEN, network access, and payment for applicable Actor usage.
The remote Actor implementation is not bundled; extraction behavior and data availability depend on external services.
Designed for public US location data, not private, authenticated, or paywalled sources.
The helper only parses JSON and returns JSON; it does not validate the input schema locally or directly export CSV.

use_cases.title: Compare Housing Locations
use_cases.description: Compare walking, transit, and cycling scores for a shortlist of public property addresses.

use_cases.title: Build Neighborhood Research Tables
use_cases.description: Collect city scores and neighborhood rankings for an initial mobility comparison, then verify important results against their sources.

use_cases.title: Enrich Public Listing Data
use_cases.description: Add declared mobility score fields to public listing datasets using small, repeatable Apify runs.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One City
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up Seattle, WA using byCity with maxItems set to 1. Show available walking, transit, and cycling scores with their labels.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Public Addresses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use byAddress for these public addresses: [addresses]. Limit results to [count] and compare available mobility scores, leaving missing values unfilled.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare a small address list.

prompt_templates.title: Review City Neighborhoods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use byCity for [city, state] with includeNeighborhoods enabled and maxItems set to 25. Summarize returned neighborhood rankings without inventing missing scores.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect city and neighborhood context.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a State Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a byState lookup for [state] with maxItems set to [limit]. Explain estimated service costs before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: after cost approval, use asynchronous execution if needed, confirm completion, and retrieve the dataset as JSON.

output_examples.input: Describe the fields expected from a city lookup.
output: Location fields: address, location type, city, state, and ZIP code.
Mobility fields: walking, transit, and cycling scores with rating descriptions.
Additional fields: nearby amenities and source URL, when supplied by the Actor.

output_examples.input: Prepare a small Seattle lookup with neighborhood context without running it.
output: Mode: byCity. City: Seattle, WA. Include neighborhoods: enabled. Record limit: 25.
Execution requires APIFY_TOKEN and an Apify account with applicable usage charges.
No lookup has run, so no current scores are reported.

best_practices: Start with a small record limit and review Apify pricing before approving larger runs.
Submit only public location inputs and keep APIFY_TOKEN out of prompts, input files, and shared output.
Verify source URLs, missing fields, and run completion before using results for comparisons or downstream datasets.
anti_patterns: Passing cookies, session credentials, private account data, or unrelated files as lookup input.
Treating missing scores as zero or presenting illustrative values as verified current results.
Starting large runs without reviewing costs, site terms, and applicable legal restrictions.

faq.question: What do I need before running a lookup?
faq.answer: You need an Apify account, APIFY_TOKEN, and network access. The bundled helper also requires Node 18 or later.

faq.question: Which locations can I request?
faq.answer: The input schema supports US addresses, cities, neighborhoods, state city tables, and national city rankings.

faq.question: Does the skill calculate the scores locally?
faq.answer: No. It requests results from a remote Apify Actor. The supplied files do not include the Actor implementation.

faq.question: Can I export results as CSV?
faq.answer: The helper and documented retrieval examples return JSON. CSV requires a separate conversion or export step.

faq.question: Are lookups free?
faq.answer: Apify bills Actor usage to your account. Check the Actor Pricing tab before running requests.

faq.question: How should I handle larger requests?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous workflow and confirm the run has completed before retrieving its dataset. Keep record limits within the input schema.
